adultGuide.title: Shelf Marker Story Theme Adult Guide: ____________________.
setupSteps: Set out one theme card, six blank paper strips, and a pencil before the adult-led session begins: ____________________.
Label the strips story question, repeated clue, character choice, ending echo, theme line, and shelf marker note: ____________________.
Choose one pretend story world and keep every name, setting, clue, and choice invented: ____________________.
Tell the writer that dictated words, copied adult wording, or independent writing all fit the paper-only activity: ____________________.
Place the finished strips under the shelf marker note so the theme can be reread without sharing it outside the session: ____________________.
facilitationNotes: Start with the story question when the writer needs a clear theme path: ____________________.
Use the repeated clue to point back to the same idea without asking for a polished sentence: ____________________.
Ask for one character choice that shows what matters in the fictional story: ____________________.
Save the ending echo until the writer can connect the ending to the first story question: ____________________.
Let the theme line stay simple, plain, and adult-supported: ____________________.
safetyNotes: Use invented characters, broad pretend settings, and made-up clues only: ____________________.
Keep the activity offline, paper-only, adult-led, and free from outside audiences: ____________________.
Skip any prompt that starts to ask for writer facts, group labels, or outside-session details: ____________________.
Avoid outside titles, creator names, service forms, labels from real shelves, or correction marks: ____________________.
Treat the theme line as a fictional story idea, not a claim about a real person: ____________________.

themeRoutines.title: Story Question Marker: ____________________.
themeRoutines.useWhen: Use when a writer needs one clear question to guide the theme: ____________________.
steps: The adult places a blank strip under the story question label: ____________________.
The adult asks what the invented story keeps wondering about: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: The story question is ____________________.
The adult rereads the question and saves it for the later theme line: ____________________.

themeRoutines.title: Repeated Clue Trail: ____________________.
themeRoutines.useWhen: Use when the theme needs a small clue that can appear more than once: ____________________.
steps: The adult points to the story question strip and asks what small pretend clue could remind everyone of it: ____________________.
The writer names one repeated clue, such as a color, object, sound word, or tiny action from the fictional world: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: The repeated clue is ____________________.
The adult helps place the repeated clue beside the story question without adding real details: ____________________.

themeRoutines.title: Character Choice Sort: ____________________.
themeRoutines.useWhen: Use when the writer needs the theme to show through action: ____________________.
steps: The adult asks which invented character makes a choice that matters: ____________________.
The writer chooses one simple action the character can take on paper: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: The character choice is ____________________.
The adult asks how that choice answers or changes the story question: ____________________.

themeRoutines.title: Ending Echo Match: ____________________.
themeRoutines.useWhen: Use when the ending needs to connect back to the first theme idea: ____________________.
steps: The adult rereads the story question and repeated clue in order: ____________________.
The writer names a calm ending moment that echoes the same idea: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: The ending echo is ____________________.
The adult checks that the ending echo matches the character choice instead of starting a new story: ____________________.

themeRoutines.title: Theme Line Builder: ____________________.
themeRoutines.useWhen: Use when the strips are ready to become one plain theme line: ____________________.
steps: The adult lays out the story question, repeated clue, character choice, and ending echo strips: ____________________.
The writer points to the strip that best shows the theme: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: The theme line is ____________________.
The adult helps trim the theme line to one simple fictional story idea: ____________________.

themeRoutines.title: Shelf Marker Close: ____________________.
themeRoutines.useWhen: Use at the end of a paper session to file the theme neatly: ____________________.
steps: The adult reads all five theme strips in order without adding new facts: ____________________.
The writer chooses a short shelf marker note that names the theme focus: ____________________.
The writer completes this line: The shelf marker note is ____________________.
The adult stacks the strips together for private paper reuse in a later session: ____________________.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Story Question Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Ask for one invented question the fictional story keeps returning to.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Repeated Clue Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Choose a pretend clue that can appear more than once on paper.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Character Choice Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Keep the choice simple and fictional.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Ending Echo Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Connect the ending back to the story question.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Theme Line Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Use plain words and one fictional idea.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Shelf Marker Note Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Make the note short enough to fit on a paper marker.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Clue Return Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Use this only to strengthen the theme, not to add more plot.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Choice Reason Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Accept dictated wording if the writer knows the idea but not the sentence.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Theme Check Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.prompt: The story question and ending echo match because ____________________.
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Reread both strips before filling the blank.

takeHomeThemeSlips.title: Paper Close Slip
takeHomeThemeSlips.prompt: This paper theme set belongs with the shelf marker note ____________________.
takeHomeThemeSlips.adultNote: Close by stacking the slips for private adult-led reuse.

optionalAdultPrompts: Which story question feels easiest to answer with a fictional character choice: ____________________.
What repeated clue could appear at the beginning and near the ending echo: ____________________.
Which character choice shows the theme without explaining it too much: ____________________.
What ending echo would remind us of the same story question: ____________________.
How can the theme line use plain words instead of a long explanation: ____________________.
What shelf marker note would help an adult find this theme again on paper: ____________________.
Which strip should the writer dictate while the adult writes: ____________________.
Which blank strip can stay empty until the story question is clearer: ____________________.
